MYTWIN / GETTING STARTED

Your first session.

From installing the studio to exporting your first take. Everything you need to get moving.

Install Fikr Vox

Fikr Vox is a desktop app for macOS on Apple silicon. Packaged downloads are not published yet; you can build the app from source.

What you’ll need

  • A Mac with Apple silicon.
  • Node.js 22 or newer and npm.
  • Rust and Xcode command-line tools.
  • An internet connection for dependencies and model downloads.

Run from source

git clone https://github.com/bigmints/vox-studio.git
cd vox-studio
npm install
npm run desktop

The first launch may take longer while the native app and its dependencies build.

Create an app bundle

npm run build:desktop

The build creates src-tauri/target/release/bundle/macos/Fikr Vox.app. Open it directly or copy it into Applications.

A local build is not a signed, notarized release. Follow macOS’s security prompts for software you have built and trust; do not disable system security protections.

For future packaged downloads, visit GitHub Releases.

Create your first project

  1. Open Fikr Vox and choose New or New project.
  2. Choose a format: Story Telling, Podcast, or Video Dubbing.
  3. Add your script. For a podcast, assign dialogue to the appropriate speaker.
  4. Choose a twin or voice and configure its engine in voice settings.
  5. Generate a take, listen to it, and adjust the words or delivery as needed.
  6. Export your audio or dubbed video when you’re happy with the result.

Projects save locally as you work. Cloud generation only begins when you invoke the relevant action.

Voices & connections

Use a local voice

Open Settings → Connections to manage local voice engines and download models. Kokoro offers preset voices; the Qwen3 options include reference cloning and other voice modes. The app shows the choices supported by each model.

Download a model before your first generation. Models vary in size, memory use, language support, and speed.

Create a twin

Open My Twin and add or edit a profile. Import a voice reference, or record a sample using the app’s microphone control. Preview the sample before saving, then choose a compatible cloning model.

Only use voice and appearance references you have permission to use. An open-source app license does not grant rights to someone else’s voice or likeness.

Connect a cloud provider

  1. Open Settings → Connections.
  2. Choose Connect beside OpenRouter and enter your key.
  3. Use Manage → Model choices to select chat, speech, and transcription models.
  4. Refresh models to load the provider’s available options.

Cloud capabilities depend on the chosen model. A speech model does not necessarily support voice cloning. Provider usage charges apply separately.

Build a podcast

Podcast projects keep dialogue on one conversation timeline, with a separate track for each speaker.

Set up your speakers

Open Speakers & voices to assign a twin or preset voice to each speaker. You can add up to seven guests alongside the host.

Import dialogue

Choose Import script and use speaker labels matching your characters. For example:

Host: Welcome to our first conversation.
Guest: Let’s make something worth listening to.

Generate and shape the conversation

Use Generate missing voices to process the dialogue. Matching completed takes can be reused. Keep the app open during generation; Stop after current turn stops further submissions after the active take finishes.

Choose Quick exchange, Natural conversation, Relaxed conversation, or Original timing. Conversation modes remove quiet padding around turns and set a gap between speakers. Manual trims and explicit positions take precedence.

Export

Preview the complete conversation or individual turns. Adjust track volume and mute controls, then choose Export audio to create a mixed WAV.

Dub a video

  1. Create a Video Dubbing project and upload an MP4, MOV, or WebM. H.264 MP4/MOV is recommended on macOS.
  2. Select your twin and write the narration. Optional transcription can help you start from the source audio.
  3. Generate the voice take and set its start time.
  4. Choose natural pace or fit-to-video timing, then render a preview.
  5. Preview and download the dubbed MP4.
Dubbing replaces all original audio. It preserves the footage, duration, and orientation, and does not change lip movements.
SettingBehavior
Natural paceKeeps the voice speed. Rejects narration that would be cut off.
FitAdjusts voice speed between 0.5× and 2×.
Source videoUp to 512 MB and two hours.
Source transcriptionUp to ten minutes and 20 MB of extracted WAV.

Local video processing requires macOS and Xcode command-line tools. Codec support follows macOS AVFoundation.

Storage & privacy

Desktop projects, imported references, and completed outputs are stored under ~/Library/Application Support/com.bigmints.fikr.vox/.

Local voice engines run on your Mac. Cloud writing, transcription, speech, and video actions send the relevant inputs to your selected provider. Review that provider’s terms before uploading sensitive content.

Provider credentials are stored locally in an owner-readable file, without encryption at rest. Keep backups private and remove secrets before sharing diagnostic files.

The browser prototype stores data separately in the repository’s data/ directory. Its data is not automatically imported into the desktop app.

Troubleshooting

A voice model isn’t ready

Check Settings → Connections and complete the model download. Verify available storage and memory, then try a smaller model if necessary.

A cloud request fails

Check the connection, key, provider credit balance, and the selected model’s capabilities. Review the provider’s activity before retrying a failed or interrupted paid request.

A video won’t import or render

Check its duration and size, try an H.264 MP4/MOV, and confirm that Xcode command-line tools are installed. Fit timing only supports 0.5×–2× voice speed.

Need more help?

Open a GitHub issue with the steps to reproduce the problem, your macOS version, and the relevant error. Remove API keys and private media before sharing logs.

Make it your own

The desktop backend uses Rust and Tauri. The interface uses plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in the system webview. Explore the source repository to contribute.

npm test
npm run test:rust

Keep changes focused, describe the behavior they improve, and include relevant verification when opening a pull request.

MIT licensed

Third-party libraries, downloaded models, and connected services have their own licenses and terms. The app’s MIT license does not replace those.
